extracted.intended_audience: users and programmers of PARI/GP (mathematicians, number theorists) who write GP scripts or use the PARI library
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for using PARI/GP library and GP functions: numerical routines, linear algebra, lattice/ quadratic-form tools, summation/integration, plotting primitives, and GP control statements. Gives function semantics, flags, constraints, and cautions for correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolvemod0 / gaussmodulo / gaussmodulo2
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve linear congruence system ∑i mi,j xj ≡ yi (mod di). Returns a small integer solution x (or 0 if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: integer matrix m, vector d of positive integer moduli, y integral column vector; y or d may be given as a single integer to apply to all components. If flag=1, returns [x, u] where u's columns form a basis of the homogeneous solutions so all solutions are x plus integer combinations of u. Library syntax matsolvemod0(m,d,y,flag); aliases gaussmodulo(m,d,y) (flag=0) and gaussmodulo2(m,d,y) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsupplement (suppl)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrix x whose columns are linearly independent, extend its columns to a full basis of the space by finding a square invertible matrix whose first columns are those of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If columns of x are not independent, an error is issued. Library syntax suppl(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mattranspose (gtrans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose of a matrix or vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation x~ or function gtrans(x). Has effect only on vectors and matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfgaussred / sqred
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition of a quadratic form (symmetric matrix q) into a sum of squares representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is a matrix whose diagonal entries are coefficients of the squares and non-diagonal entries represent bilinear forms; q(x) reconstructed from output as described. Library syntax sqred(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfjacobi (jacobi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute eigen-decomposition for a real symmetric matrix x using Jacobi's method: returns [eigenvalues_vector, orthogonal_matrix_of_eigenvectors].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax jacobi(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflll / lll family (LLL reduction) — flag semantics and numeric cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the LLL algorithm to the columns of matrix x; returns a square transformation matrix T such that x·T is an LLL-reduced basis of the lattice spanned by columns of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Flags control numeric mode and preconditions:
- flag=0 (default): computations with reals (fast) but currently numerically unstable in v2.0.19.
- flag=1: assumes corresponding Gram matrix integral — uses integer arithmetic (accurate and reasonably fast); x need not be full rank.
- flag=2: like flag=1 but x should be integer and columns linearly independent; does a partial reduction before LLL — often faster when row scales differ.
- flag=3: all computations in rationals (accurate but extremely slow); deprecated.
- flag=4: x integral but not necessarily full rank; returns [kernel_basis, LLL_reduced_Z-basis_of_image].
- flag=5: like 4 but x may have polynomial coefficients.
- flag=7: older version of flag=0.
- flag=8: same as 0 but x may have polynomial coefficients.
- flag=9: variation on flag=1 using content.
Library syntax qflll0(x,flag,prec); simpler wrappers lll(x,prec) (flag=0), lllint(x) (flag=1), lllkerim(x) (flag=4). Note numeric instability warning for flag=0 in current version.

rubrics_metrics.name: qflllgram (lllgram) — Gram-matrix LLL reduction and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: LLL algorithm applied to a Gram matrix x (square symmetric real matrix), returning transformation matrix T converting coefficients with respect to initial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Flags similar to qflll with slight differences:
- flag=0: numerically unstable in present version.
- flag=1: integer entries, computations in integers.
- flag=4: integer entries, returns kernel and reduced image.
- flag=5: same as 4 for generic x.
- flag=7: older version of flag=0.
Library syntax qflllgram0(x,flag,prec); wrappers lllgram(x,prec), lllgramint(x) (flag=1), lllgramkerim(x) (flag=4).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfminim / minim / fincke_pohst (minimal vectors) — flag semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Find minimal vectors (short vectors) of a positive definite quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix x depending on flag and bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0 (default): seeks vectors of x-norm squared ≤ b, up to 2m vectors; returns [number_of_vectors, maximum_norm_found, matrix_of_vectors] (one per ±v pair). If flag=1: ignores m and returns the first vector whose norm < b. For flag=0 or 1, x assumed integral and b=0 searches minimal non-zero vectors. If flag=2: x may be non-integral real but b=0 is meaningless and uses Fincke–Pohst algorithm. Library syntax qfminim0(x,b,m,flag); aliases minim(x,b,m), minim2(...), fincke_pohst(x,b,m,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfperfection (perf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the perfection rank of a positive definite integer quadratic form x: the rank of family of symmetric matrices vivt where vi are minimal vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware computations can be extremely lengthy when x has many minimal vectors; older versions failed when >5000 minimal vectors. Library syntax perf(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfsign (signat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the signature of the quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix x as a two-component vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax signat(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: setintersect
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute intersection of two sets x and y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In PARI a set is a row vector with strictly increasing entries. Library syntax setintersect(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setisset
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether x is a set (row vector with strictly increasing entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns 1 if x is a set, 0 otherwise. Use Set to convert vectors to sets. Library syntax setisset(x) returning a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: setminus
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute difference of two sets x and y: elements of x not in y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax setminus(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setsearch (membership / insertion index) — flag behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Search whether y belongs to sorted set x and return index semantics depending on flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If y ∈ x and flag omitted or zero, returns index j with x[j]=y; otherwise returns 0. If flag non-zero, returns index j where y should be inserted (and 0 if y already in x). Meant for use with listinsert. Works also on sorted lists. Library syntax setsearch(x,y,flag) returning a long integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: setunion
rubrics_metrics.description: Union of two sets x and y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax setunion(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: trace (gtrace)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace operation generalized to many types: for matrices, ordinary trace; for scalars equals x + conjugate(x); for polmods use algebraic number field trace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is a non-square matrix (but not a vector), an error occurs. Library syntax gtrace(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecextract / matextract / extract (component extraction modes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract components from a vector or matrix x according to a component specifier y (integer mask, vector of indices, or string describing ranges); optional z for column specifier when x is a matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If y is integer: read binary bits right-to-left mapping to components left-to-right (mask). If y is a vector: entries are component indices in that order. If y is a string: single index (negative indices count from end), range 'a..b' with omitted endpoints defaulting to 1 and -1; supports reverse order if b<a. If string begins with '^', take complement of indices. If z present, x must be matrix with y specifying rows and z columns. Examples provided. Library syntax extract(x,y) or matextract(x,y,z).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsort / sort / indexsort / lexsort (sorting semantics & flags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort a vector x in ascending order using heapsort; k parameter specifies component or lexicographic keys; flag bits change behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
x must be vector with integer/real/fraction components. k can be integer (sort by k-th subcomponent) or vector (lexicographic by listed components). Flag binary digits:
• bit1 (value=1): indirect sort — return permutation indices that sort x (use with vecextract to reorder).
• bit2 (value=2): sort by ascending lexicographic order.
Helper wrappers: sort(x)=vecsort0(x,NULL,0); indexsort(x)=vecsort0(x,NULL,1); lexsort(x)=vecsort0(x,NULL,2). Also sindexsort and sindexlexsort return a C-long integer vector of indices (not a valid PARI object but convenient for C). Library syntax vecsort0(x,k,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: numerical integration guidance (intnum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for using numerical integrators (Romberg-like) and intnum function for smooth integrands on [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
User should not expect extreme accuracy (18–28 decimal digits OK). Must remove singularities inside interval and at boundaries via analytical cleanup or change of variable. For improper integrals with infinite limits, integrand must decay sufficiently rapidly; choose a large finite bound instead of extreme representations like 1e4000 to avoid underflow. Integrand may be complex- or vector-valued. Flags:
• flag=0 (omit): for moderate a,b, smooth everywhere including endpoints.
• flag=1: general driver (slower).
• flag=2: tailored when a or b are infinite (requires ab>0; if b=+∞, prefer a≥1).
• flag=3: integrand allowed to be undefined but continuous at an endpoint (e.g., sin(x)/x at 0).
Library syntax intnum0(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix (matrix creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create m×n matrix whose entries are given by expression expr as function of row and column indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal parameters X (rows from 1..m) and Y (cols 1..n) available in expr. If last three parameters omitted, fill matrix with zeros. Library syntax matrice(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: prod (product loop) — initialization type forcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute product ∏_{X=a..b} expr with initialization parameter x used to force computation type (integer, real, power series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set x to integer 1 for exact integer arithmetic, 1. for reals at default precision, or 1+O(X^k) for power series with precision k. Example shows dramatic performance/size difference when using power-series initialization. Library syntax produit(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: prodeuler
rubrics_metrics.description: Product over primes between a and b (initialized at real 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal parameter X ranges over primes; library syntax prodeuler(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: prodinf (infinite product) — stopping criterion and flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute infinite product starting at X=a; evaluation stops when relative error of expression−1 < default precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressions must evaluate to complex numbers. If flag=1, compute product of (1+expr) instead. Library syntax prodinf(...) or prodinf1(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: solve (root finding with Brent's method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a real root of expr between a and b provided expr(a)*expr(b) ≤ 0 using Brent's method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can fail if expr undefined anywhere on [a,b] (e.g., avoid solve over intervals where tan(x) undefined). Library syntax zbrent(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: sum (finite sum) with initialization parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute sum_{X=a..b} expr with initialization x used to force computation type (similar to prod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialization allows forcing exact/rational/real/power-series arithmetic; examples show dramatic differences (e.g., summing 1/i as rational produces huge denominator). Library syntax somme(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumalt (alternating series summation) — algorithm & caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical summation of an alternating series expr starting at X=a using specialized acceleration algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses algorithm of F. Villegas modified by D. Zagier (preferred over Euler–Van Wijngaarden); flag=1 uses a variant with different polynomials (sometimes faster). Stopping criterion is based on term size, so terms exactly equal to 0 must be removed. Divergent alternating series or nearly alternating series can sometimes be summed. Performance hint: rewrite (−1)^X as (1. - X%2*2) for speed. Library syntax sumalt(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdiv (divisor sum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum expression expr over positive divisors of integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arithmetic functions like sigma exploit multiplicativity, but current version lacks a way to declare expr multiplicative in n, so prefer specialized built-ins when available. Library syntax divsum(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: suminf (infinite sum) — stopping criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute infinite sum of expr starting at X=a; evaluation stops when relative error < default precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressions must evaluate to complex numbers. Library syntax suminf(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumpos (positive-term series summation) — Van Wijngaarden trick & caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical summation of series with same-sign terms starting at X=a using Van Wijngaarden acceleration (converts to alternating series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm is slow; stopping criterion is term size so zero terms must be removed. flag=1 uses alternate polynomials sometimes faster. Library syntax sumpos(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: vector / vectorv (vecteur / vvecteur) — creation of row/column vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a row vector of n components with components given by expr evaluated at integers 1..n (vector), or a column vector (vectorv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If optional parameters omitted, fill with zeros. Library syntaxes vecteur(...) and vvecteur(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotting philosophy: high-level vs low-level and intended scope
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI provides high-level plotting functions (ploth* family) for quick plotting and low-level 'rectplot' primitives (plot* prefix) for manual drawing into up to 16 virtual rectwindows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plotting was intended as simple visual aid, not heavy-duty graphics — use specialized packages for serious work. All plotting functions are available only in GP (not in the PARI library). Under X11, plotting runs in a forked process so GP session remains usable. PostScript output is supported via ps* functions and is appended to psfile (default ./pari.ps); users should remove or change psfile to avoid appending old drawings. Initialize rectwindows with plotinit and manage scaling with plotscale. Virtual cursor semantics and window preservation described; use plotkill to erase and free memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot (ASCII crude plot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw a crude ASCII plot of expr on [a,b] with optional Ymin and Ymax bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Ymin/Ymax omitted, use minima/maxima of computed values.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotbox
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw rectangle outline in rectwindow w between current virtual cursor (x1,y1) and (x2,y2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only part inside window w drawn; virtual cursor does not move.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotclip
rubrics_metrics.description: Clip content of rectwindow w to displayable area (remove parts not visible on screen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful with plotcopy to prepare scratchpad before committing final picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcolor
rubrics_metrics.description: Set default drawing color in rectwindow w (X11 only) choosing from limited palette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Palette mapping: 1=black,2=blue,3=sienna,4=red,5=cornsilk,6=grey,7=gainsborough. Can hardwire more colors by editing rect.h and plotX.c. Library syntax plotcolor(w,c).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcopy
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy contents of rectwindow w1 to w2 with offset (dx,dy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compose complex drawings from multiple rectwindows.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcursor
rubrics_metrics.description: Return current (scaled) position of virtual cursor for rectwindow w as a 2-component vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax plotcursor(w).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Physically draw specified rectwindows placed at given physical positions; argument is a vector whose number of components is divisible by 3: [w1,x1,y1,w2,x2,y2,...].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Windows considered transparent and overlapping regions drawn twice. After assembling, drawing displayed in a special window. Use plotdraw(list).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotfile
rubrics_metrics.description: Set output file for plotting output; special filename '-' redirects to same place as PARI output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax plotfile(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: ploth (high-precision plotting) — flags and n parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: High-precision plot of y=f(x) on [a,b]. Opens window and returns bounding box [xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax].
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Advice: reduce current numeric precision (e.g., to 9) before calling ploth to reduce function-call overhead. n selects number of reference points (0 uses defaults: 1000 general, 1500 parametric, 15 recursive). Flags bits:
• 1: parametric plot (expr must be vector with even components; pairs are coordinates).
• 2: recursive plotting: adaptive subdivision using midpoint checks; fast and often more precise but can fail if unlucky or few reference points (e.g., odd functions on symmetric intervals). Other flag bits toggle display options: 8=do not print x-axis, 16=do not print y-axis, 32=no frame, 64=only plot reference points, 256=use splines interpolation, 512=no x-ticks, 1024=no y-ticks, 2048=plot all ticks same length.

rubrics_metrics.name: plothraw
rubrics_metrics.description: High-precision scatter plot of points given by listx and listy vectors of equal length; automatic uniform scaling on x and y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, join successive points. Library syntax plothraw(listx,listy,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: plothsizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Return data describing output window in a 6-component vector: window width, height, tick sizes horizontal/vertical (for gnuplot interface), character width and height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily intended for gnuplot interface; use to determine device bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotinit / plotscale (rectwindow initialization and scaling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize rectwindow w to width x and height y and set virtual cursor to (0,0); plotscale sets local coordinates mapping x1..x2 and y1..y2 to the rectwindow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plotinit destroys any existing rect objects in w. Device imposes upper bounds for x,y available via plothsizes. Example provided to initialize to maximal size using plothsizes and mapping to [0,1000]×[0,1000]. After plotscale, coordinates reflect scaled mapping; default y-axis orientation is downwards until plotscale called.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotkill
rubrics_metrics.description: Erase rectwindow w and free its memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reuse w must reinitialize (initrect/plotinit). There is no partial erase: erase completely and redraw what you want to keep.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw polygon defined by vectors X and Y (equal length) in rectwindow w; if flag non-zero, close polygon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entire polygon drawn (not just part inside w). X and Y may be scalars to draw a single segment from current virtual cursor to (X,Y); in that case only the portion inside w is drawn, and virtual cursor moves to (X,Y) even if outside window. Use plotmove to reposition cursor first if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotlinetype
rubrics_metrics.description: Change type of lines subsequently plotted in rectwindow w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: type=-2: frames, -1: axes, larger values other types. w=-1 changes high-level plotting. Mostly relevant to gnuplot interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotmove
rubrics_metrics.description: Move virtual cursor of rectwindow w to absolute position (x,y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax plotmove(w,x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotpoints / plothraw equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw points with coordinates in vectors X and Y inside rectwindow w; virtual cursor does not move (unless X,Y are scalars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X and Y scalars, draw single point and move virtual cursor to that location. plothraw is similar but does automatic scaling; plotpoints may use plotscale or no scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotpointsize / plotpointtype
rubrics_metrics.description: Change visual size and type of points plotted in rectwindow w (or all windows with w=-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only effective in gnuplot interface. plotpointtype: type=-1 corresponds to a dot; larger values map to other shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrbox / plotrline / plotrmove / plotrpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative-geometry drawing primitives: draw rectangle, line segment, move cursor, or draw point relative to current virtual cursor by offsets dx,dy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All operate relative to current cursor position (x1,y1). plotrbox draws outline of rectangle between (x1,y1) and (x1+dx,y1+dy). plotrline draws portion inside w and moves cursor to (x1+dx,y1+dy). plotrmove moves cursor relative. plotrpoint draws point at (x1+dx,y1+dy) if inside w and moves cursor there.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrecth / plotrecthraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Write to rectwindow w the curve(s) produced by ploth (plotrecth) or plot graph(s) from provided data (plotrecthraw).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plotrecth(w,X=a,b,expr,flag,n) writes output of ploth into rectwindow w. plotrecthraw(w,data,flag) expects data as a vector of vectors: for parametric, even number of vectors as coordinate pairs; otherwise first vector is x coords and remaining vectors y coords for multiple curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotscale (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set mapping of local coordinates of rectwindow w to desired x and y intervals allowing inverted ranges (x2<x1 or y2<y1 allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to change default pixel-count scaling and to reorient axes; call after plotinit for device-independent coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotstring (text placement and justification bits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw a string x at current cursor position in rectwindow w with justification controlled by flag bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag bits control alignment: bits 1&2 horizontal: left=0,right=2,center=1. Bits 4&8 vertical: bottom=0,top=8,vertical-center=4. Bit16/32 insert small horizontal/vertical gap. See tutorial for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotterm
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the terminal for high-resolution plots (handled by gnuplot driver).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using gnuplot, possible terminals same as gnuplot; term='?' lists possible values. Terminal options and size may be appended (e.g., 'gif=300,200'). Positive return indicates success.

rubrics_metrics.name: ps* functions (psdraw, psploth, psplothraw)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce PostScript output appended to psfile instead of on-screen drawing; psdraw analogous to plotdraw, psploth to ploth, psplothraw to plothraw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output appended to psfile (default ./pari.ps). Useful when plotting routines are not enabled for screen output since PostScript output can still be created.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP-only plotting restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic functions are available only inside GP, not in the PARI library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: PARI not designed for heavy-duty graphics; plotting implementation forks under X11 and frees non-graphical memory in child. Use specialized graphic packages for serious graphical work; PARI plotting intended as convenient lightweight visual aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: break (control statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupt execution of current sequence and exit immediately from n innermost enclosing loops in current function call or top-level loop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter n defaults to 1 and must be >1 to exit multiple nested loops; if n greater than number of enclosing loops, all loops exited.

rubrics_metrics.name: for (simple for-loop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Loop with formal variable X ranging from a to b and execute sequence seq for each value; nothing done if a>b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a and b must be real numbers (R). Syntax for(X=a,b,seq).

rubrics_metrics.name: fordiv (loop over divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: fordiv(n,X,seq): loop with X ranging over positive divisors of integer n, evaluating seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n must be integer type.

rubrics_metrics.name: forprime (loop over primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: forprime(X=a,b,seq): X ranges over primes between a and b inclusive; nothing done if a>b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a and b must be real; includes endpoints if prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: forstep (step-sequence loop with vector steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: forstep(X=a,b,s,seq): iterate X from a to b incrementing by s each step; s can be scalar or a vector of steps [s1,...,sn] whose successive elements are used cyclically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing done if s>0 and a>b or s<0 and a<b. s must be nonzero real or vector of steps. Example given illustrating alternating step sizes.
